question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The correct answer is B, "1940s,". The phrase "an operation that Helen Brooke Taussig helped develop in the 1940s" is a nonrestrictive appositive that interrupts the main sentence between its subject, "shunt," and its verb, "remains." Such an interrupter is set off by a pair of commas; the first comma appears after "shunt," so the blank needs the matching second comma to close it. Without that comma (A), the interrupter runs straight into the verb. A semicolon (C) would have to separate two independent clauses, but "remains a standard treatment …" has no subject of its own and is not independent. A colon (D) would wrongly announce the rest of the sentence as a list or explanation.

_meta.anchor: Helen Brooke Taussig — pediatric cardiologist; Blalock-Thomas-Taussig shunt; paired-comma interrupter

passage: Pediatric cardiology owes one of its foundational operations to a mid-century collaboration at Johns Hopkins. The Blalock-Thomas-Taussig shunt, an operation that the cardiologist Helen Brooke Taussig helped develop in the 1940s ______ remains a standard treatment for infants born with a serious cyanotic heart defect.
